Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Microbes, most of them bacteria, have populated this planet since long before animal life developed and they will outlive us.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 早在动物出现之前很久，微生物就已遍布地球，而且它们还会比我们存续得更久。微生物中大多数是细菌。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Invisible to the naked eye, they are ubiquitous.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 它们虽肉眼不可见，却无处不在。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: They inhabit the soil, air, rocks and water and are present within every form of life, from seaweed and coral to dogs and humans.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 它们生活在土壤、空气、岩石和水中，也存在于每一种生物体内，从海藻、珊瑚到狗和人，无一例外。
column6: every form of life|每一种生命形式

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: And, as Yong explains in his utterly absorbing and hugely important book, we mess with them at our peril.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 而正如扬在这本引人入胜又极为重要的书里所说，随便干预微生物，我们自己就要承担风险。
column7: at our peril|由自己承担危险

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Every species has its own colony of microbes, called a ‘microbiome’, and these microbes vary not only between species but also between individuals and within different parts of each individual.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 每个物种都有自己的微生物群，称作“微生物组”。这些微生物不仅因物种而异，同一物种的不同个体之间、同一个体的不同部位之间也有差别。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: What is amazing is that while the number of human cells in the average person is about 30 trillion, the number of microbial ones is higher — about 39 trillion.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 令人惊奇的是，平均每个人体内约有30万亿个人体细胞，微生物细胞还要多，约有39万亿个。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: At best, Yong informs us, we are only 50 per cent human.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 扬告诉我们，我们顶多只有一半算是人。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Indeed, some scientists even suggest we should think of each species and its microbes as a single unit, dubbed a ‘holobiont’.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 事实上，一些科学家甚至主张，把每个物种及其共生微生物看作一个整体，称为“全生物体”。
column9: holobiont|n. 全生物体；共生整体

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: In each human there are microbes that live only in the stomach, the mouth or the armpit and by and large they do so peacefully.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 每个人体内都有些微生物只生活在胃里、口腔里或腋下，而且总的来说都相安无事。
column6: by and large|总体上；大体上

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: So ‘bad’ microbes are just microbes out of context.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 因此，所谓“坏”微生物，不过是出现在了不合适环境中的微生物。
column5: out of context|脱离了合适的环境

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Microbes that sit contentedly in the human gut (where there are more microbes than there are stars in the galaxy) can become deadly if they find their way into the bloodstream.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 有些微生物在人的肠道中安然栖居，那里微生物的数量比银河系里的恒星还多；一旦它们进入血液，却可能致命。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: These communities are constantly changing too.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 这些微生物群落也一直在变化。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: The right hand shares just one sixth of its microbes with the left hand.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 右手上的微生物中，仅六分之一也是左手上有的。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: And, of course, we are surrounded by microbes.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 当然，我们四周也遍布微生物。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Every time we eat, we swallow a million microbes in each gram of food; we are continually swapping microbes with other humans, pets and the world at large.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 每次进食，我们吃下的每克食物都带有一百万个微生物；我们也在不断地与其他人、宠物和周围整个世界交换微生物。
column8: the world at large|外部的整个世界

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: It’s a fascinating topic and Yong, a young British science journalist, is an extraordinarily adept guide.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 这是个令人着迷的话题，而年轻的英国科学记者扬是一位格外称职的向导。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Writing with lightness and panache, he has a knack of explaining complex science in terms that are both easy to understand and totally enthralling.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 他的笔调轻快，文采飞扬，尤其善于把复杂的科学知识讲得通俗易懂又扣人心弦。
column5: has a knack of|特别善于

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Yong is on a mission.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 扬写这本书有一个明确的目标。
reviews|v. 评论；撰写书评: on a mission|一心要达成某个目标

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Leading us gently by the hand, he takes us into the world of microbes — a bizarre, alien planet — in a bid to persuade us to love them as much as he does.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 他轻轻牵着我们的手，领我们走进微生物世界。这是一个奇异而陌生的星球，而他想让我们像他一样爱上微生物。
reviews|v. 评论；撰写书评: Leading us gently by the hand|轻轻牵着我们的手
column7: in a bid to|试图；为了

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: By the end, we do.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 读到最后，我们果真爱上了它们。
microbes|n. 微生物: do|v. 代指前文的“爱它们”

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: For most of human history we had no idea that microbes existed.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 在人类历史上的大部分时间里，我们根本不知道微生物的存在。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: The first man to see these extraordinarily potent creatures was a Dutch lens-maker called Antony van Leeuwenhoek in the 1670s.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 17世纪70年代，一位名叫安东尼·范·列文虎克的荷兰镜片匠，成为第一个看到这些影响非凡的生物的人。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Using microscopes of his own design that could magnify up to 270 times, he examined a drop of water from a nearby lake and found it teeming with tiny creatures he called ‘animalcules’.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 他用自己设计的显微镜观察附近湖里的一滴水，显微镜最高可放大270倍。他发现水里满是微小的生物，便称它们为“微小动物”。
microbes|n. 微生物: of his own design|自行设计的
column10: animalcules|n. 微小动物（历史用语）

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: It wasn’t until nearly two hundred years later that the research of French biologist Louis Pasteur indicated that some microbes caused disease.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 直到将近两百年后，法国生物学家路易·巴斯德的研究才表明，有些微生物会引起疾病。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: It was Pasteur’s ‘germ theory’ that gave bacteria the poor image that endures today.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 正是巴斯德的“病菌学说”让细菌背上了坏名声，这种印象一直延续到今天。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Yong’s book is in many ways a plea for microbial tolerance, pointing out that while fewer than one hundred species of bacteria bring disease, many thousands more play a vital role in maintaining our health.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 从许多方面看，扬的书都在呼吁人们宽容对待微生物。他指出，致病细菌不足一百种，而帮助我们维持健康的细菌却有成千上万种。
reviews|v. 评论；撰写书评: in many ways|从许多方面看
column5: microbial tolerance|对微生物的宽容态度
column9: play a vital role in|在……中起关键作用

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: The book also acknowledges that our attitude towards bacteria is not a simple one.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 这本书也承认，我们对细菌的态度并不简单。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: We tend to see the dangers posed by bacteria, yet at the same time we are sold yoghurts and drinks that supposedly nurture ‘friendly’ bacteria.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 我们往往会注意到细菌带来的危险，可与此同时，商家又向我们推销据说能滋养“友好”细菌的酸奶和饮品。
microbes|n. 微生物: dangers posed by|由……带来的危险
column5: at the same time|与此同时

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: In reality, says Yong, bacteria should not be viewed as either friends or foes, villains or heroes.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 扬说，实际上，不宜把细菌简单看成朋友或敌人、反派或英雄。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Instead we should realise we have a symbiotic relationship, that can be mutually beneficial or mutually destructive.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 我们应该认识到，人和细菌是共生的；这种关系既可能对双方有益，也可能彼此有害。
column7: destructive|adj. 有害的；具有破坏性的

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: What then do these millions of organisms do?
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 那么，这数以百万计的生物究竟有何作用？

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: The answer is pretty much everything.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 答案是，它们几乎什么都做。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: New research is now unravelling the ways in which bacteria aid digestion, regulate our immune systems, eliminate toxins, produce vitamins, affect our behaviour and even combat obesity.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 新的研究正在揭示细菌如何帮助消化、调节免疫系统、清除毒素，以及如何制造维生素、影响我们的行为，甚至对抗肥胖。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: ‘They actually help us become who we are,’ says Yong.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: “它们实际上帮助我们成了今天的我们，”扬说。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: But we are facing a growing problem.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 但我们正面临一个日益严重的问题。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Our obsession with hygiene, our overuse of antibiotics and our unhealthy, low-fibre diets are disrupting the bacterial balance and may be responsible for soaring rates of allergies and immune problems, such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 对卫生的过分执着、滥用抗生素，以及不健康的低纤维饮食，正在破坏我们体内的细菌平衡，也可能是过敏及炎症性肠病（IBD）等免疫问题发生率飙升的原因。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: The most recent research actually turns accepted norms upside down.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 最新的研究其实颠覆了人们过去普遍接受的观念。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: For example, there are studies indicating that the excessive use of household detergents and antibacterial products actually destroys the microbes that normally keep the more dangerous germs at bay.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 例如，有研究表明，过度使用家用清洁剂和抗菌产品，反而会消灭那些通常能遏制更危险病菌的微生物。
column10: at bay|处于受控制的状态

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Other studies show that keeping a dog as a pet gives children early exposure to a diverse range of bacteria, which may help protect them against allergies later.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 另一些研究显示，家里养狗让孩子很早就能接触到多种多样的细菌，这或许有助于防止他们日后出现过敏。
column5: a diverse range of|多种多样的

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: The readers of Yong’s book must be prepared for a decidedly unglamorous world.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 读扬这本书的人要有心理准备：书中描绘的世界实在不怎么光鲜。
column6: unglamorous|adj. 不光鲜的；缺乏魅力的

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Among the less appealing case studies is one about a fungus that is wiping out entire populations of frogs and that can be halted by a rare microbial bacterium.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 其中一些案例读来没那么讨喜。一个案例讲的是一种真菌：它正使青蛙种群整群消亡，而一种罕见的细菌可以遏止这种真菌。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Another is about squid that carry luminescent bacteria that protect them against predators.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 另一个案例讲的是鱿鱼：它们身上带有能发光的细菌，能够借此躲避捕食者。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: However, if you can overcome your distaste for some of the investigations, the reasons for Yong’s enthusiasm become clear.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 不过，如果你能克服对某些研究的反感，就不难理解扬为何如此热衷于这个领域。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: The microbial world is a place of wonder.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 微生物世界令人惊叹。
microbes|n. 微生物: a place of wonder|令人惊叹的世界

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Already, in an attempt to stop mosquitoes spreading dengue fever — a disease that infects 400 million people a year — mosquitoes are being loaded with a bacterium to block the disease.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 为防止蚊子传播登革热，已经有人让蚊子携带一种能阻断传播的细菌。登革热每年会导致四亿人感染。
reviews|v. 评论；撰写书评: in an attempt to|为尝试做……

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: In the future, our ability to manipulate microbes means we could construct buildings with useful microbes built into their walls to fight off infections.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 展望未来，我们对微生物的调控能力意味着，我们也许能建造这样的楼宇，把有益的微生物纳入墙体来抵御感染。

Wendy Moore reviews Ed Yong’s book about: Just imagine a neonatal hospital ward coated in a specially mixed cocktail of microbes so that babies get the best start in life.
温迪·穆尔评埃德·扬关于微生物的著作。: 想象一下，在医院的新生儿病房里，病房内的表面覆盖着专门调配的多种微生物，好让婴儿获得最佳的人生开端。
column9: get the best start in life|获得最佳的人生开端
